products.name: CAFE FADUCCI OMNI Colombia, Excelso Las Moras, Natural 200g
products.description:
A naturally processed coffee from Las Moras in Pitalito, Huila, grown at elevations between 1,700 and 1,900 metres. This lot combines careful cherry selection and controlled processing to create a rich, expressive cup with vibrant fruit character, depth, and complexity.

TASTES LIKE: Blackberry Compote, Shiraz, Ribena

PRODUCER: Las Moras
REGION: Pitalito, Huila
VARIETAL: Caturra, Bourbon Amarillo, Colombia
PROCESS: Natural
ALTITUDE: 1700–1900 masl

STORY
Colombia Excelso Las Moras is cultivated in the renowned Pitalito region of Huila, Colombia, an area celebrated for its rich coffee heritage and ideal growing conditions. Situated at elevations ranging from 1,700 to 1,900 metres above sea level, the region provides an excellent environment for producing high-quality specialty coffee.

The varieties used in this coffee include Caturra, Bourbon Amarillo and Colombia, each contributing to the distinctive character of the Las Moras lot.

The processing of Colombia Excelso Las Moras follows a carefully controlled method designed to preserve quality and build complexity. Freshly harvested cherries are thoroughly sorted to remove underripe fruit, leaves and debris, ensuring that only the best cherries continue through processing.

The cherries then undergo a 24-hour oxidation period, allowing the coffee to develop greater aromatic complexity before moving through the remaining processing stages.

Finally, the coffee undergoes controlled mechanical drying, helping stabilise the beans while preserving the flavour compounds developed throughout the process. The result is a coffee with body, intensity and complexity that reflects the care taken at every stage.

ORIGIN
Pitalito, Huila, Colombia
Pitalito is one of the most recognised coffee-producing areas in Huila and is widely regarded as one of Colombia’s leading specialty coffee regions. Its high elevations, fertile soils and cool mountain climate allow coffee cherries to mature slowly, supporting the development of sweetness, acidity and complexity.

Huila has earned an international reputation for expressive and high-quality coffees, with Pitalito playing an important role in that recognition. The combination of favourable growing conditions and meticulous farming and processing practices continues to make coffees from this region highly sought after within the specialty coffee industry.

products.name: CAFE FADUCCI OMNI Ethiopia, Halo Beriti, Washed 200g
products.description:
A Grade 1 washed coffee from Halo Beriti Washing Station in Yirgacheffe, Ethiopia. Produced from carefully selected cherries delivered by local smallholder farmers, this Special Prep lot undergoes repeated hand-sorting throughout receiving and drying to ensure exceptional quality and clarity.
⠀
TASTES LIKE: Floral, Citrus, Earl Grey
⠀
PRODUCER: Halo Beriti Washing Station / Smallholder Producers
REGION: Yirgacheffe
VARIETAL: Heirloom Ethiopian Varieties
PROCESS: Washed
ALTITUDE: 2100–2300 masl
⠀
STORY
Halo Beriti Washing Station was established in 2014 and serves 750 smallholder producers, who deliver their coffee in cherry form.
⠀
This particular lot is part of a “special preparation” in which hand-sorting was done repeatedly throughout the receiving and drying process, ensuring that only perfect coffees made it into the bags.
⠀
With the special prep, what producers generally call “Premium” in Ethiopia, cherries are collected from a limited number of smallholder farmers. Around 90% of the cherries are perfectly picked at the correct red colour, with approximately 5% semi-red and 5% overripe. These cherries are processed and stored separately from other lots, with only a small number of bags produced this way each year.
⠀
The coffee is typically picked ripe and depulped the same day. Fermentation generally lasts 8–12 hours in open-air tanks before the coffee is washed in water channels to remove the mucilage. The seeds are then spread on raised beds to dry for approximately 5–15 days, depending on the weather.
⠀
ORIGIN
Yirgacheffe, Ethiopia
Yirgacheffe is renowned for producing distinctive and complex coffees. The region’s thick vegetation is supported by a warm tropical climate with moderate wet and dry seasons, while most coffee is shade-grown by small producers using organic practices.
⠀
Coffee is cultivated between approximately 1,600 and 2,400 metres above sea level across the Yirgacheffe highlands. The large number of microregions and washing stations contributes to a wide range of cup profiles and expressions.
⠀
Ethiopia holds a unique position in the coffee world as the birthplace of Arabica coffee. Coffee cultivation, processing, and consumption have been part of everyday life for centuries, with many producers cultivating coffee on very small plots that function more like coffee gardens or forest environments than conventional farms.
⠀
The majority of Ethiopian producers are smallholders, often farming less than one hectare of land. These producers commonly deliver freshly picked cherries to nearby washing stations, where coffees are sorted, processed, and dried before export.

products.name: CAFE FADUCCI OMNI Peru, Utcubamba, Washed 200g
products.description:
A farm-traceable washed Gesha microlot from producer Ricarte Rojas Oblitas in Peru. Grown on his 0.75-hectare farm at 1,750 metres above sea level, this lot reflects careful hand harvesting, precise washed processing, and a strong commitment to environmental stewardship.
⠀
TASTES LIKE: White Peach, Pear, Green Grape
⠀
PRODUCER: Ricarte Rojas Oblitas
REGION: Utcubamba, Amazonas
VARIETAL: Gesha
PROCESS: Washed
ALTITUDE: 1750 masl
⠀
STORY
Ricarte Rojas Oblitas owns a 0.75-hectare farm located in the Utcubamba province of the Amazonas department. The farm is home to around 3,200 Gesha trees.
⠀
Ricarte grows coffee with passion, carrying out the entire process under technical guidance. His coffee is washed processed after being carefully harvested by hand.
⠀
Caring for the environment is important to his work. He conserves the forest trees on the farm to better protect the land and produces his own compost as fertiliser. Within the community, he also contributes to environmental stewardship.
⠀
His long-term goals are to sell directly to customers in other countries and achieve a better quality of life.
⠀
This coffee is part of Café Imports’ Peru Microlot program. Microlots from Peru are traceable to the farm level and represent some of the highest-quality coffees selected from individual producers.
⠀
ORIGIN
Utcubamba, Amazonas, Peru
Utcubamba is located in the Amazonas department of northern Peru, where Ricarte Rojas Oblitas’ farm is situated. The farm sits at 1,750 metres above sea level and is planted with around 3,200 Gesha trees.
⠀
The PDF separately lists Cajamarca as the coffee’s region, while its producer profile specifically places the farm in Utcubamba province, Amazonas. For this listing, Utcubamba, Amazonas is used because it is the most precise farm-location information provided in the source.
⠀
Washed processing is common in Peru. Coffees are typically depulped on the day of harvest, fermented for around 12–18 hours in open-air tanks, washed clean of mucilage, and then dried using methods such as patios, raised beds, parabolic dryers, or mechanical drying.
